Shrink it, hand it off, or let it go with a kind two-line message, and put 30 minutes of something that has felt like you lately into the gap, then protect that block like a meeting. People who keep even small pockets of time for what they find meaningful report more energy and less burnout, and it starts with noticing which commitments are really yours. Ten minutes on a Sunday. hook: The clocks jump ahead Sunday. Things I will do instead of going to bed 15 minutes earlier:
text:
Daylight saving time starts this Sunday, March 14, and the Monday after is one of the roughest mornings of the year for sleep, mood and attention. Most of us know the fix and do none of it. Watching one more episode to relax before the relaxing. Reorganizing a kitchen drawer at 11:40pm. Reading about how daylight saving time works, in bed, on the phone, brightness all the way up. Setting the alarm 15 minutes earlier and calling it the same thing. The real plan is boring and it works: move bedtime and wake time 15 minutes earlier tonight, again on Wednesday and again on Friday, get 10 minutes of outdoor light each morning, and skip the Saturday late night. By Sunday your body clock has already made most of the move and the lost hour barely lands. Tag the friend who will be doing research at midnight.

hook: You brush your teeth 4 minutes a day. Make it a workout: 2 moves in the morning, 2 at night
text:
You are already standing at the sink for two minutes twice a day, so the hardest part of this workout is done. Morning, minute one: calf raises, rise onto your toes and lower slowly for the whole minute, holding the sink if you wobble. Morning, minute two: stand on one leg for 30 seconds a side, and close your eyes for the last 10 seconds if that is easy. Night, minute one: sink squats, hold the counter, sit back like you are reaching for a chair and stand tall, slow and steady. Night, minute two: standing side leg lifts, 30 seconds a side, toes pointing forward, no leaning. Calf raises help the veins in your legs push blood back up, single-leg balance is one of the better predictors of staying independent as you age, and squats are the move you do every time you get out of a chair. Modify as needed: hold on with both hands, do fewer reps, or just do the morning pair this week. Skip anything that hurts and check with your care team first if you are managing a condition. hook: Beef and broccoli in 20 minutes, 8 ingredients, and the sauce beats the takeout tub
text:

Add four cups of broccoli florets and two tablespoons of water to the same pan, cover for three minutes until bright green and just tender. Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss one to two minutes until glossy. Serve over brown rice. Feeds four. Lean beef brings iron, zinc and B12, broccoli brings vitamin C and fiber, and the low sodium soy keeps the salt far below the takeout tub. Save this for a Thursday.

hook: Your phone can speak for you when you cannot. Set up your medical ID in 3 minutes
text:
If you ever cannot speak for yourself, a paramedic or an ER nurse can read your medical ID from the lock screen without unlocking the phone, and call your emergency contact from there too. Three minutes to set up, and most people managing a condition have never done it. On an iPhone, open the Health app, tap your picture, then Medical ID, and turn on Show When Locked. On Android, open Settings and search for emergency information or medical info; on a Samsung it lives under Safety and emergency. List your conditions, every medication with its dose, allergies, and one emergency contact who actually picks up. Add anything a stranger would need in the first five minutes: blood thinners, insulin, an epinephrine pen, a pacemaker or implant, a seizure plan. Then test it: lock the phone, tap Emergency on the lock screen and check that it shows. Update it after every medication change. Ask the person you love most to set theirs up tonight, and share this with them.

text:

Serve as is, or top each bowl with a fried egg or a sausage for a full dinner. A bag of potatoes, a cabbage, scallions and a splash of milk run about six dollars and feed six, roughly a dollar a plate before the egg. hook: The doorway workout: 4 strength moves, 5 minutes, no floor, nothing to buy
text:
Every home has a doorframe, and a doorframe is a pull-up bar, a push-up bench and a squat rail if you use it right. Doorway rows: hold both sides of the frame, feet close to it, lean back with straight arms and pull your chest toward the frame, 10 reps, two rounds, and this is the pulling movement most home workouts skip. Frame push-ups: hands on the frame at chest height, step your feet back, lower your chest toward the doorway and press away, 10 reps, two rounds, further back is harder. Doorway squat hold: hold the frame lightly, sit back like you are reaching for a chair, hold 20 seconds and stand tall, three times. Finish with a chest opener, forearms on the frame, one foot stepped through, a gentle lean for 30 seconds. Modify as needed: fewer reps, a smaller lean, or just the rows and the stretch this week. Skip anything that hurts and check with your care team first if you are managing a condition or an injury. Five minutes, no floor, no equipment, and your back and shoulders will notice by Friday. hook: Spring starts tomorrow. The 20-minute indoor air reset your lungs will notice: 4 steps
text:
Spring officially starts tomorrow, and after five months of closed windows the air inside is often two to five times more polluted than the air outside. Twenty minutes fixes most of it. Open windows on two sides of the home for 10 minutes, because a cross breeze moves stale air out faster than one window open all day. Swap the furnace or HVAC filter if it has been three months, and write the date on the new one with a marker so you never have to guess again. Strip the bed and wash sheets and pillowcases on hot, then vacuum the mattress and under the bed while it is bare, since that is where dust mites spend the winter. Finish by wiping the tops of the fridge, the door frames and the ceiling fan blades, the places a winter of dust settles and waits for the first warm day to fall. If you have allergies or asthma, do the dusting with a damp cloth and keep the windows open while you work. Save this for Saturday morning.

Basket row: hinge forward with a flat back, let it hang at arm's length, pull it to your ribs and lower slowly, 10 reps. Basket carry: walk it down the hall and back twice with your shoulders down and your core tight. Rest a minute and repeat the whole thing once. hook: The patient portal message that actually gets answered: 4 lines, under 100 words
text:
A portal message that is three paragraphs long gets skimmed. One that is four lines long gets answered. Here is the shape. First line, what: since Tuesday I have had this symptom, about a 6 out of 10. One symptom, one number, one date. Second line, what you tried: took the as-needed medication twice, rested, drank more water, no change. Third line, what you want: can we adjust the dose, or should I come in? Ask a question they can answer yes or no. Fourth line, logistics: the best times to reach you and the number. Then stop. Nurses triage dozens of these a day, and short, specific and ending with a clear question gets yours to the top of the pile. If something is urgent, do not use the portal at all, call the office or go in. Save this for the next time you are staring at a blank message box.

hook: Your first outdoor workout of spring needs one park bench: 4 moves, 6 minutes
text:
Spring is here, and the gym just moved outside. Every park bench is a full set of equipment if you know four moves. Bench sit to stand: sit on the edge with your feet flat, stand up without using your hands, then sit back down slowly, ten times. Incline push-up: hands on the backrest or the seat, body in one straight line, lower your chest toward the bench and press back up, eight to ten times. Step-up: one foot on the seat or a lower step, press up to standing, step down with control, eight each leg, holding the backrest for balance if you need it. Bench march: sit tall, lift one knee and then the other with your arms swinging, 45 seconds. Rest a minute and go through the round once more. Beginner friendly, and every move has an easier version: use your hands on the sit to stand, pick a taller backrest for the push-up, use the curb instead of the seat. Modify anything that does not feel right, and if you are managing a condition check with your care team before starting something new. Morning sunlight sets your sleep clock for tonight, so these six minutes do two jobs at once.

hook: Spring is loud with plans. This Sunday, a 10-minute walk with one question
text:
April fills up fast. Plans, projects, a garden to start, a closet to clear. Before you add one more thing, take ten minutes this Sunday. Leave the phone at home, or in a pocket on silent, and walk with no destination and no podcast. Carry one question only: when this week did I feel most like myself? Notice what shows up, a person, a place, a task, a time of day, and do not try to fix or plan anything, just notice. Back home, write one line on a sticky note and stick it by the kettle. Next Sunday, read it before you walk, and ask the question again. After a month you will have four lines, and those four lines will tell you more about your purpose than any vision board. Purpose is not found in a plan. It is noticed, one week at a time, in moments you already had. Save this for Sunday.

hook: Two soup cans are a pair of dumbbells. The pantry workout: 4 moves, 6 minutes
text:
Open the pantry. Two soup cans weigh about a pound each, which is exactly where beginners should start with arm and shoulder work. Four moves, about six minutes, standing the whole time. Can curls: a can in each hand, elbows tucked by your ribs, curl up to your shoulders and lower slowly, 12 reps. Overhead press: cans at shoulder height, palms forward, press up until your arms are straight and lower with control, 10 reps. Side raises: arms by your sides, lift the cans out to shoulder height with palms down, pause, lower slowly, 10 reps. Can march: hold the cans at your chest and march in place lifting your knees for 45 seconds. Rest a minute and repeat once. Modify as needed: use water bottles, empty hands or fewer reps, keep the movements slow and smooth, and check with your care team before starting something new if you are managing a condition. When a pound feels easy, move up to a full water bottle. Save this for the next time the weather keeps you in.

hook: 4 questions at the pharmacy counter that can shrink your prescription bill
text:
Managing a condition means a standing date with the pharmacy, and the bill is not as fixed as it looks. Four questions to ask at the counter. One: is there a generic, and what is the cash price without insurance? Sometimes the cash price is lower than your copay, and the pharmacist can only run it that way if you ask. Two: is a 90-day supply cheaper per month than three 30-day fills? Often yes, with fewer trips and fewer missed doses. Three: do you have a discount card or manufacturer coupon you can run? They can check in seconds. Four: is there a similar medication on my plan's preferred list? Ask them to flag it to your prescriber. Never switch or stop a medication on your own, and if a price jump means you are skipping doses, tell your prescriber that too, because there is almost always another option. Pharmacists answer these every day and most people never ask. Save this for your next refill.

- 16 cooked large shrimp, peeled, halved lengthwise
- 1 cup shredded carrot
- 1 cucumber, cut into thin sticks
- 8 butter lettuce leaves
- 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro

- 1 tbsp hoisin sauce
- 1 tbsp lime juice
- 1 tsp low-sodium soy sauce
- 3 to 4 tbsp warm water

Steps:
1. Cover the vermicelli with boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
2. Whisk peanut butter, hoisin, lime juice and soy sauce, then thin with warm water until pourable.
3. Dip one wrapper in warm water for 10 to 15 seconds until just soft and lay it on a damp board.
4. On the bottom third, layer lettuce, a small bundle of noodles, carrot, cucumber and herbs. Set 4 shrimp halves pink side down just above.
5. Fold the bottom over the filling, fold in the sides and roll it up tight. Repeat for 8 rolls.
6. Serve with the peanut sauce. Rolls keep 1 day wrapped in a damp towel in the fridge.

4. Fry the eggs in the last teaspoon of oil over medium for about 3 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks stay runny.

Pumpkin Pie Greek Yogurt Parfait
Serves 2. Prep 5 min, cook none.

Ingredients:
- 1 1/2 cups plain Greek yogurt
- 1/2 cup canned pumpkin puree (not pie filling)
- 1 tbsp maple syrup
- 1 tsp pumpkin pie spice
- 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1/2 cup low-sugar granola
- 1/4 cup toasted pecans, chopped
- 1 apple or pear, diced (or pomegranate seeds)

Steps:
1. Stir the yogurt with the pumpkin, maple syrup, pumpkin pie spice and vanilla until smooth.
2. Layer in 2 glasses: pumpkin yogurt, granola, diced apple. Repeat.
3. Top with the toasted pecans and a pinch more spice.
4. Make ahead: the pumpkin yogurt keeps 3 days in the fridge. Add the granola just before eating so it stays crunchy.

text:
Homemade cranberry sauce in 15 minutes with no refined sugar: make it tonight, it tastes better tomorrow

Fiber and vitamin C from whole cranberries, with far less added sugar than canned.

Maple Orange Cranberry Sauce
Serves 10 (about 2 1/2 cups). Prep 5 min, cook 15 min.

Ingredients:
- 12 oz fresh or frozen cranberries (one bag, about 3 cups)
- 1/3 cup pure maple syrup
- 1 tbsp orange zest (from 1 orange)
- 1/2 cup fresh orange juice (1 to 2 oranges)
- 1/4 cup water
- 1 cinnamon stick (or 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon)
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger (optional)
- Pinch of salt

Steps:
1. Rinse the cranberries and pick out any soft ones. Zest the orange before you juice it.
2. Put the cranberries, maple syrup, orange zest, orange juice, water, cinnamon stick, ginger and salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat.
3. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer and cook 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until most of the berries have popped and the sauce thickens.
4. Mash a few berries against the side of the pan for a thicker sauce, or leave it chunky. Remove the cinnamon stick.
5. Cool 20 minutes. It thickens more as it cools. Spoon into a jar.
6. Make ahead: it keeps 10 days in the fridge and is even better after a day. Serve cold or at room temperature.
